content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have a [product_name] module and plan to operate a 12V DC solenoid valve using it. What component should I use to convert the digital output to provide a 12V DC supply? For reference, I'm using a 12V DC car battery as the power source.

Are you looking to simply turn the solenoid valve on and off? Your [product_name] features relay outputs. To wire it, connect the positive terminal from your 12V DC supply to one side of the relay output, then connect the other side of the relay output to the positive side of the solenoid valve coil. The negative side of the solenoid coil should go to the negative (or 0V DC) of your 12V DC power source.
Hello [user_name], No problem. I've attached a wiring diagram for reference.

I've encountered challenges when switching 12V DC solenoid valves using automation modules. High inrush current can damage the built-in relay contacts. I recommend using a high current relay rated at around 30A, triggered by your module, and wiring the solenoid valve through the contacts of this external relay. For example, you could try a relay model similar to Bosch 0332209150.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion revolves around controlling a 12V DC solenoid valve using a [product_name] module with relay outputs. Key insight is that while users seek simple control for 12V DC actuators, reliability issues can occur when switching loads directly, particularly from high inrush current. Practical advice is shared, including clear wiring instructions and recommendations for separate, high-current external relays for demanding loads to ensure long-term reliability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that the [product_name] module's relay outputs will operate a 12V DC solenoid valve safely and reliably, with explicit wiring guidance and avoidance of premature relay contact failure. There is a preference for solutions that combine clear instructions with robust electrical operation.
